title: SharePoint admin center: Copilot skills for step-by-step guidance and multi-criteria site search
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the feature, licensing, automatic availability and both control rows; the earlier fetch warnings were not evidence of broken links. The assertion about how commonly administrators hold Copilot licences is unsupported, and three minor qualifications need correction. Historical correction instructions embedded in the briefing were treated as history, not followed.

claims.claim: The roadmap names step-by-step task guidance and multi-criteria site search as the two new skills.
claims.quote:
We’re excited to announce two new Copilot skills in the SharePoint Admin Center:

- Step-by-Step Task Guidance

claims.claim: Copilot walks administrators through common tasks with sequential instructions.
claims.quote: Copilot recommends clear, sequential instructions to guide you from start to finish.

claims.claim: Microsoft's guidance example asks how to find potentially over-permissioned sites.
claims.quote: For example, you can ask questions like "How can I find sites that are potentially over-permissioned?"

claims.claim: The feature page says the guidance first runs the organization's site permissions report.
claims.quote: It first runs the site permissions report for your organization, then runs activity-based reports, and finally initiates site access reviews for site owners to review and remediate their sites.

claims.claim: The feature page says the guidance next runs activity-based reports.
claims.quote: It first runs the site permissions report for your organization, then runs activity-based reports, and finally initiates site access reviews for site owners to review and remediate their sites.

claims.claim: Multi-criteria site search accepts several conditions in one request.

claims.quote: Copilot generates a filtered list of sites based on your criteria.

claims.claim: The roadmap's search example is sites inactive for more than 60 days and shared externally.
claims.quote: Example: “Find sites that have been inactive for more than 60 days and are shared externally.”

claims.claim: The Learn search example is sites created in the last month and shared externally.
claims.quote: For example, you can type a query like "Find sites created in the last month that are shared externally."

claims.quote: Select the Copilot button in the upper right shell to launch Copilot in the SharePoint admin center.

claims.quote: Copilot returns details about the specific site, including site name, URL, creation date, creator, external sharing status, sensitivity labels, storage status, template, and site ID.

claims.claim: Copilot supports voice input for dictated queries.
claims.quote: Voice input enables you to dictate queries into Copilot, improving accessibility and ease of use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference requires SharePoint Advanced Management for Data access governance reports.
claims.quote: SharePoint Advanced Management (SAM) license is required to run these reports.
claims.fix: Retain the cmdlet-reference attribution. Qualify the reporting requirement in the note, prose and checklist: 'The snapshot report shown here requires SharePoint Advanced Management. The Data access governance overview also documents limited activity reporting with Microsoft 365 E5, without snapshot reports or remedial actions.' The overview is https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-reports.

claims.claim: The requirements page says SharePoint Advanced Management is available as part of Microsoft 365 Copilot or as an add-on.
claims.quote: SharePoint Advanced Management is available as part of Microsoft 365 Copilot or as an add-on.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Adding administrators to the custom security group CopilotForM365AdminExclude disables this Copilot experience for them.
claims.quote: To disable Copilot in the SharePoint admin center, set up a custom security group called CopilotForM365AdminExclude, and then add the administrators you don't want to have the Copilot experience.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Entra admin center path is Entra ID > Groups > All groups > group > Members > + Add.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Groups > All groups.
3. Select the group you need to manage.
4. Select either Members or Owners.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/groups/{group-id}/members/$ref adds a member to the exclusion security group.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/{group-id}/members/$ref
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint unchanged. Append to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'The request body sets @odata.id to the reference for the administrator being added.'

claims.claim: The Entra group-management procedure requires Groups Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You'll need the Groups Administrator or User Administrator role to add members and owners.

claims.claim: Data access governance reports are reached in the SharePoint admin center through Reports > Data access governance.
claims.quote: In the left pane, expand Reports and then select Data access governance.

claims.claim: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers -Workload SharePoint -ReportType Snapshot -Name <name> -CountOfUsersMoreThan <count> generates the report.
claims.quote: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers -Workload SharePoint -ReportType Snapshot -Name "OversharingBaselineReport" -CountOfUsersMoreThan 0

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row and following prose
claims.claim: Accessing the Data access governance reporting experience requires SharePoint administrator credentials.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center with the SharePoint administrator credentials for your organization.

claims.claim: The reporting cmdlet generates a report rather than restricting Copilot.
claims.quote: This cmdlet generates Data Access Governance (DAG) reports meant to provide insights into potential oversharing of sensitive data in SharePoint and/or OneDrive for Business.

claims.claim: The feature page documents the exclusion group but no tenant-wide admin-center switch to turn this experience off.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "SharePoint admin center" "disable" "tenant". Read the feature page's enable/disable FAQ; it gives CopilotForM365AdminExclude, not a tenant-wide UI switch. Search results about KnowledgeAgentScope concern site-level Copilot, not this admin pane.

claims.claim: The feature page states no separate meter.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot skills" "SharePoint" "pricing" "meter". Read the entire Copilot skills in the SharePoint admin center page, including its cost FAQ; it says included with a Microsoft Copilot license and names no separate meter.

claims.claim: Only a subset of administrators in most tenants hold a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "SharePoint administrators" "most" "license". Read the feature page's licensing FAQ and Microsoft Copilot requirements; neither states the prevalence of administrator licensing across tenants.
claims.fix: Remove 'which only a subset of administrators in most tenants will hold' from the cost rationale.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to check Microsoft Purview Audit, but that monitoring surface has no controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check in Microsoft Purview Audit which records appear for Copilot in the SharePoint admin center'. Table: 'Which administrators can use Copilot in the SharePoint admin center'; 'Data access governance reports'.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet beginning 'Check in Microsoft Purview Audit'. Retain the audit-event question in Open questions; do not add a control row.
